column1: Which file configures a virtual environment?

column1: Which line in pyvenv.cfg provides the isolation?

column1: What does the home line in pyvenv.cfg point at?
column2: A real Python interpreter elsewhere on disk. The environment borrows it rather than containing a copy.

column1: Why is a fresh virtual environment small?
column2: It contains no interpreter of its own — only your packages and a pointer to a real Python.

column1: What is bin called on Windows?

column1: What does activating an environment actually do?
column2: Puts that environment's bin folder at the front of your PATH, so its python is found first.

column1: Why is forgetting to activate so quiet a failure?
column2: Nothing warns you. Your shell simply finds the machine-wide python and the install lands on the shared shelf.

column1: What replaces activation when using uv?

column1: In what order does uv look for an environment?
column2: An activated VIRTUAL_ENV, then CONDA_PREFIX, then a .venv in this folder or any parent.
